update_2026_11_23_run_by_snapshot: The stated reading of item (1) above ('the file handed to report is the run') was refuted by the rival on 1c8b68a (reproducer d9c8cb31952bfb5f: a finding whose first row is of an earlier snapshot and whose second is of the report's scored 0 hits; the file is one chain over every cycle, 26a:47, and 26m:64-65 folds a fingerprint only inside a run) and is replaced in referee/harness/score.py: the run scored is the file's rows whose snapshot_id is the snapshot document's; a row of another snapshot is counted (counts.other_runs) and never read, so it is neither the first of its fingerprint nor refused, and the reason snapshot_mismatch is gone (cd referee && python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_score.py' -k Runs). The question stays open and is now sharper, because this is the narrowest run the rows can tell and it is still not a run: (a) two runs on one snapshot cannot be told apart (a row carries no run id); (b) an observation the writer writes no row for is in no run: a finding still open from an earlier snapshot (findings.write rule 7, 26k:16-18), and a planted line equal to a line already found in the same file (one fingerprint, 26m:61-62), so a case only such an observation hits is scored a miss (Runs.test_the_writer_s_file_over_two_snapshots shows the first). Asked as before: where the observations of one run are recorded, since 26k's 'a re-observation writes no row' and 26m's 'the scorer reads the writer's file' together leave a re-observed finding unreadable in the run that saw it.
